DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. Drag and drop the code snippets from the bottom onto the blanks in the code to complete the JSON request that implements the ACL presented. Not all code snippets are used.
ip access-list block_badactors
  10 deny tcp 91.213.17.6/24 199.213.12.14/16
theory: Mapping the CLI ACL 'deny tcp 91.213.17.6/24 199.213.12.14/16' into its JSON managed-object form means each field has a specific JSON attribute: the second address in a 'deny <proto> <src>/<srclen> <dst>/<dstlen>' statement is the destination, so dstPrefix must be 199.213.12.14 (matching the already-filled dstPrefixLength of 16), while srcPrefixLength must capture the /24 following the source address 91.213.17.6 — and the trailing '}' simply closes the still-open attributes object before the surrounding structure closes. Swapping the source and destination fields is the classic mistake this item is testing. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools) / (Cisco documentation / web research)
